import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales
coffee_sales['total'] = coffee_sales['price'] * coffee_sales['quantity']

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot for total sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_by_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(data=sales_by_product, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.ylabel('Product')
plt.title('Total Sales by Product in Coffee Shop')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales
coffee_sales['total'] = coffee_sales['price'] * coffee_sales['quantity']

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot for total sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_by_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(data=sales_by_product, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.ylabel('Product')
plt.title('Total Sales by Product in Coffee Shop')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
